title: nix-store-csi
description: Publishes, NAR fetches, the node store, garbage collection and prefetching of the nix-store-csi node plugins, and the locality extender.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: Node plugins that Prometheus scrapes.

panels.title: Failed publishes
panels.description: Publishes in the time range that failed with an error other than Unavailable. Unavailable means the plugin is still fetching the closure, and kubelet retries.

panels.title: Failed NAR fetches
panels.description: NAR fetches in the time range that failed. The plugin then tries the next cache.

panels.title: Paused caches
panels.description: Caches that a node skips for a minute after a failed request.

panels.title: Store size
panels.description: NAR size of the node stores, on all selected nodes.

panels.title: Publishes
panels.description: NodePublishVolume calls by gRPC status code. Unavailable means the plugin was still fetching the closure after 90 seconds.

panels.title: Publish time
panels.description: Time from NodePublishVolume to a mounted volume, for publishes that succeeded. On node means the node store already had the closure, and fetched means the publish waited for a fetch. A fetch that takes longer than 90 seconds shows up as retries of 90 seconds or less.

panels.title: Closures in flight
panels.description: Closures being resolved or fetched, by node. A closure counts until its fetches end, even after its publish returns Unavailable at 90 seconds.

panels.title: NAR throughput
panels.description: Uncompressed NAR bytes fetched, by cache.

panels.title: NAR fetches
panels.description: Tries at fetching a NAR, by cache and result.

panels.title: Fetched by cache
panels.description: Uncompressed NAR bytes that each cache served in the time range.

panels.title: NAR fetch time
panels.description: Successful NAR fetches by the time they took to download, unpack and verify. Large NARs take longer, so a slow fetch doesn't always mean a slow cache.

panels.title: NARs in flight
panels.description: NARs being fetched, by node. --max-substitution-jobs caps it.

panels.title: Store size
panels.description: NAR size of the node store, and of the part that garbage collection can't delete, by node. --max-store-size limits the second.

panels.title: Freed
panels.description: NAR size of the store objects that collection deleted in the time range.

panels.title: Deleted paths
panels.description: Store paths that collection deleted in the time range.

panels.title: Failed collections
panels.description: Collections in the time range that failed. They run every --gc-interval, 10 minutes by default, and every minute while free space or inodes are short.

panels.title: Free space over --ensure-free
panels.description: Free space on the node store's filesystem above what --ensure-free keeps, by node. It stays below 0 only once collection has deleted every unused store path older than --keep-recent, and then it deletes newer ones.

panels.title: Failed syncs
panels.description: Syncs in the time range that failed. Each one deletes the store paths it covered, and points to a failing disk.

panels.title: Prefetch rollout
panels.description: Node plugins that fetched the closure of each prefetch list, by its name and hash. A list's rollout is done once its new hash reaches the dashed line of its system, the node plugins of that system that Prometheus scrapes. With node pools, a pool's lists reach only the node plugins in that pool, and the top-level lists those outside every pool and in the pools that inherit them.

panels.title: Prefetch lists
panels.description: For each prefetch list by name and hash, the node plugins that fetched its closure, out of those that have seen it. During a rollout, the old hash's row goes away once kubelet updates the ConfigMap on every node.

panels.title: Prefetch list size
panels.description: NAR size of the closure that each prefetch list holds, by name, on the node where it is largest. The nodes that hold a list hold the same closure, so this is not a sum. During a rollout, a node holds the old version's closure until it has fetched the new one. storePaths stands for the lists without a name. A store path in several lists counts in each. Prefetched closures count towards each node's uncollectable_bytes, which the Store size panel shows and --max-store-size limits.

panels.title: Best score, kube-scheduler
panels.description: Prioritize answers to kube-scheduler by their best score, as a share of the top score, for pods whose closure has resolved. The extender never learns which node the scheduler picks, so read this next to Publishes that fetched. Mostly 0 means no candidate node held the pod's closure. High while publishes still count with fetched="true" means a candidate held it and the scheduler chose another node, because its other scores outweighed the extender's.

panels.title: Best score, Volcano
panels.description: Prioritize answers to Volcano by their best score, as a share of the top score, for pods whose closure has resolved. The extender never learns which node the scheduler picks, so read this next to Publishes that fetched. Mostly 0 means no candidate node held the pod's closure. High while publishes still count with fetched="true" means a candidate held it and the scheduler chose another node, because its other scores outweighed the extender's.

panels.title: Publishes that fetched
panels.description: Share of the publishes that succeeded which waited for a fetch, on the nodes that the Node variable selects. It counts every pod with a volume of this driver, including those of a scheduler without the extender.

targets.expr: sum ((nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK",fetched="true"} - last_over_time(nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK",fetched="true"}[15m] offset $__interval) >= 0) or nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK",fetched="true"}) / sum ((nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK"} - last_over_time(nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK"}[15m] offset $__interval) >= 0) or nix_store_csi_publish_duration_seconds_count{instance=~"$instance",grpc_code="OK"})

panels.title: Answer time
panels.description: Time to answer the prioritize requests that succeeded, by scheduler. Volcano sends every pod on each candidate node, so its requests take longer to read.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (scheduler, le) ((nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"} - last_over_time(nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"}[15m] offset $__interval) >= 0) or nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"}))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (scheduler, le) ((nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"} - last_over_time(nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"}[15m] offset $__interval) >= 0) or nix_store_csi_locality_prioritize_duration_seconds_bucket{result="ok"}))

panels.title: Failed answers
panels.description: Prioritize requests that the extender answered with 400, by scheduler. With ignorable, the scheduler places the pod without the extender's scores. Without it, Volcano leaves the task for its next session.

panels.title: Nodes read
panels.description: Nodes whose plugin the extender read within its last 3 intervals, against the node plugins that Prometheus scrapes, the dashed line. The extender scores the nodes in the gap 0.

panels.title: Scrapes
panels.description: Reads of the node plugins' /store-paths, by result, those answered with 304 too. Failed lookups of the plugins' Service count as errors.

panels.title: Closure resolves
panels.description: Closures that the extender resolved from the caches, by result. A failed resolve scores the pod 0 on every node for a minute.

panels.title: Unsynced paths
panels.description: Fetched paths waiting for a syncfs. It should drop back to 0 soon after fetches end.

panels.title: Views
panels.description: Views, one for each closure that volumes on the node use.

panels.title: Versions
panels.description: The version that each node plugin runs.
